title: Anti-exfil PSBT fields: test vectors
encoding: All byte strings are lowercase hex. PSBTs are serialized with keys sorted within each map; a reader must not depend on order.
derivation: Secret keys are SHA256("ae16/<form>/vec/<name>") for names a, b, c and internal (see each input's device_secret_keys). rho for the n-th pair drawn in an exchange is SHA256("anti-exfil psbt vector/<id>/rho/<n>"). Previous transactions are synthetic and numbered from 1 in each exchange.

classes.exchanges: host_psbt is the host's own PSBT. A host given host_psbt, the keys in device_keys and the rho values must send first_request, accept first_response, send second_request, accept second_response and produce host_result. A signer given a request must produce the response. final_transaction is host_result finalized, and was accepted and mined by Bitcoin Core on regtest (see README).
classes.signer_refusals: A signer holding the secret keys listed must fail on the request, and return nothing. reason_code is a label from the reference code; only the failure is normative. A case marked conditional applies only under the stated condition: a signer that has an ordinary signing path may return the PSBT, signed or not, but never with an anti-exfil field. A case marked optional_form needs a form the text makes optional (the Taproot script path); a signer that does not support it fails for that reason, and Jade's stated limits apply.
classes.host_refusals: The host runs the exchanges in order; the last response is tampered, or an earlier one is rejected. The host must fail the attempt, copy nothing from the response, and count one failure.
classes.host_accepts: Responses that differ from the request in an allowed way, and requests the host must go on with. The host must accept them and count no failure. Only the host is tested: the responses are those of a signer that holds a list of keys.
classes.request_refusals: The host must refuse before recording an attempt. This is not an attempt and counts for nothing. A case marked optional_form needs a form the text makes optional.
classes.lifecycle_scenarios: Host runs against one store, in order. A 'run' starts the host on host_psbt with the stated rho, answers each request with the scripted response (the word ERROR means the device failed), writes unsolicited_before to the host's input before it starts and unsolicited_after_response straight after the response, and ends the process at a request marked kill. 'expect' is the outcome and the failure count the host prints; 'requests' is the number of requests it sends. 'junk_store' writes the bytes to the store path. 'reset' asks the host to clear the count, with or without the user's confirmation. A step may carry a stop: before_rho, after_rho or outstanding:<n> (the user stops before rho is sent with nothing outstanding, after rho is sent, or while the response to request n is outstanding). A scenario with requires_contract 2 needs the reset command or the decline answers of CLI contract version 2; requires_contract 3 needs the stop option, or the choice to change the transaction after a failure (user_changes_transaction on a step).
classes.user_facts: What the user is told, as facts a log can show (CLI contract version 3, requires_contract 3). For the exchange named, a host given host_psbt tells the user it is requesting anti-exfil signing before its first request, and neither host nor signer presents the fee as verified when fee_may_be_presented_as_verified is false. A party that presents it as unverified, or does not say, passes when the field is true. An entry with approval_pairs also fixes what the signer's approval covers: approvals_per_second_pass approvals, together showing exactly the listed signatures by input, sighash type and leaf hash.

lifecycle_scenarios.rule: At startup, an attempt still recorded as open counts as failed.
At startup, an attempt still recorded as open counts as failed; an attempt that already holds a failure is not charged again.
A host that cannot read its records for a device MUST treat that device as having a count of one.
A later success on that attempt does not undo it. An acknowledgement covers exactly one new attempt and is used up in the write that records it.
A failure event is a message the host did not request. It does not end the attempt.
The host adds one at the first failure event in an attempt, and at most once per attempt.
Outside any attempt the host discards a message it did not request.
A host need not count a decline the user confirms was unrelated to what the device showed. A decline because the device showed something unexpected counts.
An attempt that already holds a failure cannot be abandoned; a confirmed decline is not retried.
The count resets only by an explicit user action that states what is being cleared.
A reset clears any pending warning.
A device error is a failure event, counted once, and a retry that succeeds completes the attempt: "A later success on that attempt does not undo it."

If the failure count has risen since the user last acknowledged a warning, the host MUST warn the user before starting another attempt with that device. Changing the message, coins or fee, reconnecting and restarting do not clear this requirement.
